person.name: Terry Lowry
person.office: Publisher, The Link Letter; radio host

verifyNote: Encoded from public reporting; each item links its source; candidate items await human confirmation. Facts only, no verdicts. The Link Letter is lawful; nothing here asserts illegality.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: Terry Lowry is a Houston-based conservative radio host who publishes The Link Letter, a Republican-primary voter guide (slate mailer) distributed to GOP primary voters that claims to identify the most conservative candidates on the ballot.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: Lowry hosts 'The What's Up Program,' a daily conservative talk radio show carried on 100.7 FM KKHT 'The Word' in Houston.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: Reporting describes The Link Letter's business model as one in which candidates can buy advertisements in the mailer in exchange for Lowry's recommendation and/or article placement, and notes that advertisers are generally candidates who received his endorsement.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: A 2012 account reported that advertisements in The Link Letter run 'as much as $10,000-15,000 each,' with candidates asked to buy ads or contribute to an associated PAC.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: In the 2018 Republican primary edition, individual candidates were reported to have paid $15,000 each for placement in Lowry's mailer.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: The Link Letter began in Harris County and has since been distributed with county-specific editions in Brazoria, Collin, Galveston, Fort Bend, Lubbock, McLennan and Tarrant counties.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: Local political reporting noted that the Hotze, Lowry and Polland slates 'have not lost an election when all three endorsed the same candidate in Harris County' up to a May 2016 primary, reflecting a very high win rate for jointly endorsed candidates.

records.subject: Terry Lowry
records.label: A Texas Ethics Commission complaint arising from 2010 advertising-disclosure allegations was settled by Lowry for $500, without any admission or denial of wrongdoing.

disputes.subject: Terry Lowry
disputes.label: Allegation (subject of a 2010 Texas Ethics Commission complaint) that The Link Letter charged two candidates different rates for the same amount of ad space; the matter was later settled without any admission or denial of wrongdoing.

disputes.subject: Terry Lowry
disputes.label: In 2014 the Harris County Republican Party passed a resolution condemning pay-to-play endorsement practices of the type associated with The Link Letter.

disputes.subject: Terry Lowry
disputes.label: Some candidates listed in Link Letter editions have publicly said they were included without paying and were unsure why they were featured, and critics have characterized the guide as misleading; these are contested characterizations, not established findings.
